title: Helicopter Specialist, AH-1Z/UH-1Y (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (6048, 6114, 6124, 6154, 6174, 6324, 6531), DC AVN
raw_text:
2. MOS 7313, Helicopter Specialist, AH-1Z/UH-1Y (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (6048,
6114, 6124, 6154, 6174, 6324, 6531), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Ground Maintenance Technicians and Aircrew are responsible
for performing duties incident to the maintenance and operation of Marine AH-
1Z and UH-1Y Aircraft. This MOS will be assigned only to qualified AH-1W and
UH-1N Maintenance Technicians and Aircrew holding 6048, 6114, 6124, 6154,
6174, 6324, or 6531.

       b.   Prerequisites.   None.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Meet all requirements/prerequisites for the primary H-1 MOS.

        (2) Complete the appropriate formal school at NAMTRAGRUMARDET, MCAS
Camp Pendleton, CA.

        (3) Complete the Maintenance Training Management and Evaluation
Programs (MATMEP) Level II asterisk items for the appropriate MOS. The Level
II asterisk items are the mandatory "Training Task" contained in the formal
school training tracks.

        (4) Aircrew must complete all requirements contained in the
appropriate NATOPS Manual or syllabi peculiar to the AZ-1Z and UH-1Y
aircraft.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to
reference (bo), Aviation Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual, and reference
(bn), Maintenance Training Management and Evaluation Programs (MATMEP) for
MOS 7313.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Air Crew Members 55-3011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

body:
OFFICERS/OPERATORS 1. Introduction. The enlisted flight crews in this OccFld assist in the planning and execution of tactical in-flight refueling and assault support missions, perform navigational duties, and operate and maintain the various communications and loading equipment in transport aircraft.

2. MOS 7313, Helicopter Specialist, AH-1Z/UH-1Y (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (6048, 6114, 6124, 6154, 6174, 6324, 6531), DC AVN a. Summary. Ground Maintenance Technicians and Aircrew are responsible for performing duties incident to the maintenance and operation of Marine AH- 1Z and UH-1Y Aircraft. This MOS will be assigned only to qualified AH-1W and UH-1N Maintenance Technicians and Aircrew holding 6048, 6114, 6124, 6154, 6174, 6324, or 6531. b. Prerequisites. None. c. Requirements (1) Meet all requirements/prerequisites for the primary H-1 MOS. (2) Complete the appropriate formal school at NAMTRAGRUMARDET, MCAS Camp Pendleton, CA. (3) Complete the Maintenance Training Management and Evaluation Programs (MATMEP) Level II asterisk items for the appropriate MOS. The Level II asterisk items are the mandatory "Training Task" contained in the formal school training tracks. (4) Aircrew must complete all requirements contained in the appropriate NATOPS Manual or syllabi peculiar to the AZ-1Z and UH-1Y aircraft. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to reference (bo), Aviation Training and Readiness (T&R) Manual, and reference (bn), Maintenance Training Management and Evaluation Programs (MATMEP) for MOS 7313.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
